section_2.title: From Secant to Tangent (1:00-2:30)
section_2.content: Visualize a position-time graph. Show a secant line connecting two points (A and B). Shrink the interval between A and B toward zero. As B approaches A, the secant line morphs into the tangent line at point A.
section_2.example: Animation of a sliding point B on a curve y=x²; as the distance 'h' shrinks, the secant slope visually approaches the tangent slope.

section_3.title: Defining the Derivative (2:30-4:00)
section_3.content: Formalize the visual logic into the limit definition: f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain the numerator as 'change in y' and denominator as 'change in x' (infinitesimal slice).
section_3.example: Using a drone's altitude function h(t) = -16t² + 100 to find the exact velocity at t=2 seconds by solving the limit.

section_4.title: Synthesis & The Big Picture (4:00-5:00)
section_4.content: Summarize that the derivative represents the 'instantaneous slope' or 'rate of change.' It is the engine behind velocity, growth rates, and optimization in physics and economics.
section_4.example: A 'Robot Factory' analogy: If the input is material, the derivative tells us exactly how fast the output (product) is being manufactured at any given millisecond.
